notes: The user reviewed the concrete dialogue proposal and requested that emoji not repeat. The implementation uses 16 distinct emoji, with one source location for each; the full source inventory is validated by tests/dialogue_emojis.mjs.

All six Level 1 gameplay branches have the agreed player question and two branch-specific Alex replies. Level 2 has clearer introduction, three-metric and six-metric exchanges. Exact text fixtures are exercised by the browser checks.

Consecutive Alex replies form one visual group with separate typing indicators; only the first shows a visible name/avatar. Later replies retain a screen-reader speaker label. The shared conversation brings a new reply into view when needed.

The Level 2 introduction now waits for a lower-right Choose three metrics button click. Its next action appears with Alex’s second message, and a real-time check confirms that waiting does not navigate automatically.
The Level 1 prediction page removes the redundant visible label/helper while retaining an accessible input name, example, character counter and valid aria-describedby target.

Level 1 begins its post-observation conversation 3500ms earlier: the old 6000–8000ms evidence interval is reduced to 2500–4500ms. A real browser timeline confirms about 2500ms for the tested preparation finding; typing and reply reading intervals are retained.

The untracked-area warning uses a stronger 1.25-second light-to-brick border pulse, a wider glow and a synchronized warning icon. Real normal-motion checks confirm ongoing animation, the new duration, thicker border and icon pulse. Reduced-motion behaviour remains static.

All 20 three-metric combinations, complete 3→6→10→25→100 flow, both levels’ name/context handoff, completion lifecycle, audio, keyboard controls, responsive layouts and fresh-page lifetime passed their respective checks.
The Level 2, Level 1 smoke and feedback suites use real presentation intervals. Partner-host, name integration and release checks advance waits with the browser clock.

The downloadable ZIP passed integrity checks and both included HTML entries match the current production builds. Offline browser checks serve the actual HTML bytes through an in-memory HTTPS origin because managed Chromium blocks local-file navigation; direct opening in the user’s particular browser was not observed.

The dialogue review covers gameplay bubbles. The teammate’s opening and finished cinematics remain separate, with Narrative V2 classroom readings as temporary placeholders. The player-name and scene-renderer contracts remain compatible. Level 3 remains reserved.
